title: Want, must, can — and the second verb
goal: Say what you want to do, have to do, and can do — and master the second-verb form that is the most common mistake learners make.
bekal: use the التزامی form after می‌خواهم، باید، and می‌توانم
talk about plans and the future

dialogs.title: گفتگو — تمدیدِ ویزا
dialogs.intro: Budi's visa is about to expire. Maryam helps him plan what to do.

notes: ⚠️⚠️ **This is the number one mistake learners make in Persian.** In "I want to go", English keeps "go" in a neutral form. Persian **changes** the second verb: می‌خواهم **بروم**, not می‌خواهم می‌روم. The second version is wrong, and it stands out immediately.
**Notice that BOTH verbs carry the same person ending.** می‌خواهم بروم ("I want I go"), می‌خواهید بروید ("you want you go"). It feels redundant to English ears, but Persian requires it.
⚠️ **The word باید never changes.** باید بروم، باید بروی، باید برود — باید stays the same for every person, and only the second verb changes. That's good news: one less word to memorize.

⚠️ **The verbs بودن and داشتن have irregular التزامی forms.** بودن → **باشم، باشی، باشد** (not ببودم). داشتن → **داشته باشم، داشته باشی، داشته باشد** (two words!). Both are very common, so memorize them now: باید آنجا **باشیم** ("we have to be there"), شاید وقت **داشته باشم** ("maybe I'll have time").

**"Don't worry" = نگران نباشید** and **"God willing, it'll work out" = ایشالله درست می‌شود** are two reassuring sentences you'll hear often from Iranians — and they're worth having ready to give back.
**Spoken forms:** باید چی کار کنم؟ (*bâyad chi kâr konam?*), می‌تونم فردا برم؟ (*mitunam fardâ beram?*), می‌خوام زود برم (*mikhâm zud beram*), نگران نباشین (*negarân nabâshin*).

grammars.title: The second-verb form: التزامی
body: The formula is exactly the same as the command form in unit 13: **بـ + present stem + person ending**, and **no** می. Example with رفتن (stem رو):
after: **Negative: replace بـ with نـ.** نروم ("that I not go"), امیدوارم نیاید ("I hope he doesn't come").

**Compound verbs drop the بـ altogether:** کار کنم (not بکار کنم), and likewise صحبت کنیم and تماشا کنید. Only the کردن/شدن part changes, and that's where بـ would attach — but with کردن it's usually dropped in compounds.
⚠️ **Two irregular forms you must memorize:** بودن → **باشم**, and داشتن → **داشته باشم**. Both come up in almost every conversation about plans.

after: Notice that **می‌خواهم، باید، می‌توانم themselves stay in their normal form**; only the second verb changes. And باید doesn't change at all.
⚠️ **A common mistake:** می‌توانم می‌آیم (wrong) — the right form is می‌توانم بیایم. A quick check: **if two verbs come in a row, the second one almost certainly can't take می**.

grammars.title: Asking permission, offering help, suggesting
after: **The lightest way to ask permission is می‌شود ...؟**, and it's the one you'll hear most. Spoken: می‌شه ...؟ (*mishe...?*). It works for anything: می‌شه اینجا عکس بگیرم؟ ("can I take a picture here?").

blocks.text: **The word ایشالله ends almost every plan**, just like *inshallah* across the Muslim world, with the same layers of meaning: sincere, but leaving room. Even non-religious Iranians use it out of habit.

blocks.title: Verbs that require التزامی — a list for your wall
items: Triggers: می‌خواهم · باید · نباید · می‌توانم · نمی‌توانم · شاید · بهتر است · لازم است · امیدوارم · می‌شود · بگذارید · بیایید · قصد دارم · تصمیم گرفتم · تا (so that) · برای اینکه (so that) · قبل از اینکه (before)
Every word on this list has one thing in common: **the verb after it can't take می.** If you're unsure mid-conversation, remember this short rule: *two verbs in a row → the second takes بـ*.

blocks.title: Five sentences for any office
items: "Excuse me, I've come to extend my visa." — ببخشید، برایِ تمدیدِ ویزا آمده‌ام.
"What documents are needed?" — چه مدارکی لازم است؟
"When is my turn?" — نوبتم کِی است؟
"Could you say that again?" — می‌شود دوباره بگویید؟
"Where do I need to sign?" — کجا باید امضا کنم؟ All five sentences use التزامی or forms you already know — spot which ones yourself.
